name: magnet-button
title: Magnet Button
description: A button that leans toward the finger from a field around it and presses on release.

perf.budget: Touch moves retarget two springs on the UI thread; nothing runs at rest.

a11y.reducedMotion: The button stays put and only dims slightly while the finger is over it.
a11y.touchTarget: At least 52 pt tall; the field adds 40 pt of reach on every side.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { MagnetButton } from '@/components/kinetik/magnet-button';

<MagnetButton onPress={start}>Get started</MagnetButton>;
```

Touching anywhere in the field around the button (40 pt by default) pulls it toward the finger. Releasing over the button presses it; releasing elsewhere lets it spring back.

## When to use

- A hero call to action with space around it: landing, onboarding, empty states.
- Playful products where the button can invite the finger in.

## When not to use

- Tight layouts. The field reaches into neighbouring elements and needs room.
- Rows of buttons. Fields overlap and the pulls compete.

## Notes

- The field uses negative margins, so it does not change your layout. Give the button at least `field` points of free space on each side.
- The touch tracking never claims the gesture, so the button works inside scroll views.
- Reduced motion keeps the button still and only dims it under the finger.
- The button sizes to its label. Position it with `style`, e.g. `style={{ alignSelf: 'center' }}`.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add magnet-button`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
